summary: 1. One new meeting note: a Weekly Review Meeting (7-Sep) not previously ingested. 2. Weekly commitment keeps declining for a third straight week - 440 tons two weeks ago, 414 last week, now 402 - against this week's 64,000-ton target with roughly 50,000 projected. 3. Leadership wants a recovery plan, not repeated justification. 2. 4. A proposed Stage 4/5 sequencing resolution: hold the current ramp and deplete Stage 4 ore first (finishing the 740 level south, winding up Stage 4 north to ~730m, then returning south), rather than let Stage 5 north development cut the ramp that serves Stage 4. 5. High-grade ore window narrows to roughly 12 days before Stage 4 bottom must be accessed. 3. 6. A blast filled the Stage 5 ramp with spillage (did not overflow above the ramp). 7. Clearance plan: two machines work the edge for ~2 hours with a catchment berm maintained, consistent with this KB's standard overspill controls. 8. Stage 4 port access expected to close 5-6 days while blocks 505/506 are blasted. 4. 9. Truck availability metric dispute surfaces: the team runs 21 of 24 trucks, reporting ~96% availability on the 21-truck denominator - a figure leadership (Dominic) disputes, since the full 24-truck denominator drops it to ~80-85%. Separately, "Machine 253" is named down for electrical issues, expected back this week - a description that does not obviously match this KB's standing EX-253 record (Swing Bearing Failure since 28-Jul, Week 38 repair forecast). ROM feed data: the flat-boulder fragment from the first ~5m of each Stage 5 cut (named at the 110th pass) now carries a loader-delay figure (5-10 min/cycle plus hammer backlog). A competing fragmentation fix surfaces - reducing Stage 5 blast benches from 10m to 5m - distinct from the top-cut-separation proposal already open. 6. 2027 budget planning opens with three volume scenarios (22M / 26M / 30M tons) under review; the team leans toward 30M (Stage 6 extension, more equipment and people) against a backdrop of high OPEX. 7. The diesel-refueling thread (110th pass's GM-level directive) gets its first visible follow-up: Jacobus Johannes Swart asks the maintenance team to inspect the fuel bay for a second dispensing nozzle. Inspection-scheduling only, no timeline yet - consistent with, not contradicting, the 110th pass's Done-status mismatch finding on the same task. 8. Task Feedback Log: no unprocessed rows this pass - the 19 rows the 110th pass closed out earlier the same day remain the most recent, all Processed. Important References folder re-checked: 37 files, no new or updated content since the 105th/107th/108th/109th/110th passes' last check.
